minutes.headline: Finance Committee heard FY20 budget requests from Council on Aging, Library and Land Use; no budget votes taken.
minutes.summary: The committee heard FY20 budget presentations from the Council on Aging, the Library and the land use department, which covered the building permit software and a master plan request. Members discussed the senior tax work-off program, library state-aid rules, and how fees fund the permit software. They approved the January 24 minutes and adjourned; the financial director reported the ClearGov transparency site is nearly ready.

public_comment.topic: A resident urged the town to raise the senior tax work-off cap and hourly pay toward the state maximum, since only six people are participating.
Asked about the 6% rise in the Conservation salary line and how fee revenue will offset the permit software cost.
A resident urged attention to OPEB liability through contract negotiations and asked for a full cost analysis, including recurring costs, of the fuel tanks versus a fleet card.

budget_items.what_was_said: Director asked for a small amount above level funding for the annual donation to the nutrition provider.

budget_items.topic: Council on Aging grants and donations
budget_items.what_was_said: Memory cafe program has received grants and donations since September.
Resident noted the state maximum is higher than the town offers and that funds set aside went unused.
Library asked for a near-flat increase, slightly above the town manager's target.
Friends gave money, plus fines and state aid, bringing actual spending above the town budget.
Assessment has climbed and a further annual increase is expected.
State removed fines from the formula, lowering the required municipal appropriation.
Friends pay for museum passes, supplies and programs.
Budget is on the town manager's target, mostly salaries.
Maintenance cost is lower than expected and will be partly funded by a 5% permit technology fee.
Original request was reduced so the plan could be funded over two years.

decisions.decision: Chair will take time at the end of each meeting to collect questions to carry to the March 28 public hearing, including a cost-benefit analysis of the fuel tanks.

what_happened.line: The Finance Committee heard FY20 budget requests from the Council on Aging, the Library and the land use department; no budget votes were taken.
The Library described a near-flat request, and said a state change to the aid formula lowers the municipal appropriation it must meet.
Land use said its budget is at the town manager's target and that permit software maintenance will be partly paid by a permit technology fee.
A resident urged raising the senior tax work-off cap and hourly pay toward the state maximum, noting few people take part.
The chair said time would be set aside at each meeting to collect questions for the March 28 public hearing, including a cost-benefit analysis of the fuel tanks.

why_it_matters: FY20 requests from these departments feed the town budget, mostly taxes, and the senior tax work-off terms and the permit fee decide who pays for services and software.
Fuel tanks and OPEB liability were raised as questions for a full cost analysis, which bears on long-term costs that fall on the tax bill.
watch_next: March 28 public hearing, where the questions collected at these meetings, including the fuel tank cost-benefit analysis, are to be carried.
